ranking.note: Raised to P1: removes the cs_main dependency from index sync, fixes startup/reindex race conditions returning stale data, and unblocks out-of-process indexing (#10102) and wallet rescan reuse (#15719) — the category-defining decoupling work.
Moved up from score position 6: data integrity comes first in this category and this is the only PR stopping an index from reporting corrupt/unreadable data as a plain 'missing transaction'.
Placed ahead of #26966 because it is the stated foundation work that parallel sync builds on.
Strong long-standing user request, but ranked below the integrity fix and the sync-time work per the category's ordering.

inconsistencies: Chain order: #34489 (batched index writes) extracts the foundation that #26966 (parallel index workers) builds on, and #34489 itself depends on merged #34897. Review #34489 first; reviewing #26966 in isolation risks re-litigating the batching design.

#35728 and #34132 attack the same class of problem — read/deserialization failures masked as 'not found'. #35728 is squarely in the index path (TxIndex/GetTransaction) and should be reviewed first; #34132 is mostly coins/dbwrapper (validation territory) with index reads as a side effect, which is why it sits a band lower here despite similar framing.

#36002 (pruned txindex) and #36480 (txospenderindex compact keys) both refactor the block-sequence/key-format helpers introduced by merged #35531 out of txindex for shared use. They will collide textually and conceptually; #36002 has the larger stated consumer and should set the shared-helper shape.

#24230 (indexes access node state via interfaces, no cs_main) and #35474 (index ownership moved from globals into NodeContext) are two halves of the same decoupling direction and touch the same call sites. #24230 is the broader and more consequential of the two and should be decided first so #35474 can be rebased onto whatever ownership model it establishes.

#35229 converts CBlockIndex pointers to references across chain/index/net code; it will conflict mechanically with #24230, which removes CBlockIndex from the index interfaces entirely. Its band already reflects that it is the lower-value of the pair.
result.notes: No PR here reports an active corruption or user-visible wrong answer being served to light clients, so the band distribution is deliberately top-light: one P1 for the decoupling/race-fix work that several other efforts depend on, a P2 cluster covering integrity-of-error-reporting, sync time, and the pruned-txindex feature, and P3/P4 for housekeeping and janitorial refactors. #34132's index impact is real but secondary to its chainstate scope, which is outside this category.
